decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun no later than the  expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

Reason: In order to comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
description:
Site and Surroundings  
The application site comprises the rear garden of an existing residential property. At present, a small brick structure is located at the far end of the garden. The garden is arranged over several levels and contains a number of established trees in proximity to the location of the existing structure.

Proposed Development  
The proposal involves the demolition of the existing brick structure at the end of the garden and its replacement with a new garden building in a similar location. In addition to the replacement building, the proposal includes alterations to the garden landscaping in order to rationalise and improve the existing stepped arrangement of levels.

The uppermost tier at the end of the garden will be extended to provide a more functional level area. A retaining wall will be constructed to support this tier. Below this, a new intermediate planting bed will be created, followed by a further retaining wall which will form a level patio seating area adjacent to the main dwelling.

Design Approach  
The design approach seeks to replace the existing structure with a new garden building that sits comfortably within the garden setting while improving the overall usability of the outdoor space. The reconfiguration of the garden levels will provide clearer zones for planting and seating while retaining the overall stepped character of the garden.

Given the proximity of existing trees, careful consideration has been given to the foundation design. The proposed building will be supported on screw pile foundations with a reinforced raft slab forming the base. This approach minimises excavation and helps reduce potential disturbance to nearby tree root systems.

Access  
Access to the garden building will remain via the existing dwelling and garden. The regraded garden levels and new patio area will improve circulation and usability of the garden space.

Overall, the proposal represents a modest improvement to the existing garden environment through the replacement of the current structure and the enhancement of the garden’s layout and functionality.
